questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The story of Romeo and Juliet
How to write a hit song
Why teenagers shouldn't fall in love
Love, heartbreak and how music can help
questions.why: They meet a singer-songwriter who used music to express love and mend her broken heart.

questions.q: How did Sam feel when she first fell in love at fourteen?
options: As if every love song was written for her
Confused and worried about her feelings
Too embarrassed to tell anyone at school
She stopped liking love songs completely
questions.why: She says it seemed every word of every love song had been written just for her.

questions.q: Why did Julia Jacklin move to London?
options: To study music
To join a new band
To be with her boyfriend
To find a better job
questions.why: She bought a one-way ticket to London to be with her boyfriend.

questions.q: What happened after things went wrong in London?
options: She went straight back home to Australia
Her feelings became songs on her first album
She stopped making music for several years
She rejoined her old band from school
questions.why: She poured her feelings of lost love into songs that became her first album.

questions.q: What did Julia find heartbreaking when she was young?
options: Adults not believing young love was real
Her parents' divorce when she was twelve
Losing her best friends after moving away
Her first band's failure to get a deal
questions.why: She says 'adult cynicism about love' was very heartbreaking for her at that age.

questions.q: What would Julia tell her younger self now?
options: Be careful and don't trust love
Listen to the adults
Wait until you are older
Go for it!
questions.why: She says she'd probably just say, 'yeah – go for it!'

questions.q: What does Dr Lucy Brown wish someone had told her?
options: That true love always lasts forever
That heartbreak happens, but you recover
That young people should avoid love
That music cures heartbreak quickly
questions.why: She says go for it, but heartbreak happens, and 'you're gonna get over it'.

questions.q: How is Dr Brown's view different from Julia's?
options: She thinks young love is silly and pointless
She is completely against falling in love
She says go for it, but be more realistic
She thinks adults should decide for teenagers
questions.why: She thinks we need to be more realistic about falling in love, while still saying 'go for it'.
